profiles.argument: The complete family corresponds exactly to Borsh 0.10.4 among all 55 assessed stable releases. It rejects zero-sized elements before reading, reports length-read errors before the hint, returns an empty vector for zero length, preserves the u8 reader specialization, and otherwise applies cautious after the length read and before allocation/element callbacks. The model represents the truncating cast and its panic: positive size 2^32 with nonzero length consumes the header then invokes the panic callback without allocation or element calls; size 2^32 + 1 computes capacity using divisor 1. No upper bound is added. Earlier implementations differ in zero-sized-element handling and/or byte-buffer allocation; 0.10.0–0.10.3 and 0.11.0 allow zero-sized elements and decode one such element for nonzero length, while 0.10.4 rejects them before reading. All 1.x use the different InvalidData/Collections zero-sized error profile. Existing callback, allocation and cleanup boundaries are preserved. The diagnostic-allocation exclusion is shared with other library models. The singleton is the result of the complete release/source review, not a baseline pin.
conditions: The index callback interprets the actual <T as BorshDeserialize>::deserialize_reader::<&[u8]> (or Self::deserialize) implementation, including its result, remaining slice, state effects, unwind and terminal exits.

The index element selects u8 (whose vec_from_reader override is used) or an implementation with the default vec_from_reader, together with size_of::<T>(); the binding establishes that choice for the actual T and target layout.

The allocation provider interprets Vec::with_capacity, push, vec![0u8; n] and resize at the reported sizes, including allocation failure (an abort on Solana); Vec::new() for length 0 is infallible and not reported. Deallocation of a dropped partial vector is not reported.

The division-panic callback interprets the actual panic strategy and effects, retaining unwind state or terminal reason, at the remaining slice after the u32 length read. Its Empty return value rules out returning normally. It runs before vector allocation and element callbacks whenever the generic path has nonzero length and a positive size divisible by 2^32.
Destructors of decoded values dropped on error paths are not represented; the binding establishes that they have no observable effect in the model state.
The shared package boundary excludes custom-allocator failure during construction of errors and diagnostics.

The full family has no size upper bound. Only the separate pure/returning adapter requires the substantive proof size = 0 or size % 2^32 != 0, so its division-panic branch is unreachable; that adapter condition does not restrict the family or its compatible release set.

profiles.argument: The complete bool slice-decoder operation corresponds in all 22 stable 1.x releases under the shared error-construction boundary. One read_exact reads the fixed scalar width; the reached helper translates UnexpectedEof to InvalidData, "Unexpected length of input". Every 0.x operation differs: versions before 0.6.0 expose UnexpectedEof or older permissive bool behavior; 0.6.0–0.9.3 use the explicit fixed-slice deserialize predecessor and 0.10.x/0.11.0 use deserialize_reader, with InvalidInput rather than InvalidData. Exactly one byte is consumed. Tags 0 and 1 decode to false and true; any other tag returns "Invalid bool representation: N" with the decimal byte N and the profile-specific error kind. Before 0.2.10 every non-1 byte is accepted as false; through 0.2.5 even empty input returns false. Success advances the slice by the scalar width. The contract deliberately leaves the remaining slice after an error unconstrained: the pinned std read_exact empties a short slice, while the predecessor and Borsh no_std implementation retain it. No additional reader callback domain is admitted by the predecessor mapping, and it does not create a registered older callable binding.

profiles.argument: The complete bool slice-decoder operation corresponds in all 19 listed releases under the shared error-construction boundary: Borsh 0.6.0–0.9.3 uses the explicit fixed-slice BorshDeserialize::deserialize predecessor; 0.10.0–0.10.4 and 0.11.0 use deserialize_reader with R = &[u8]. Both return InvalidInput, "Unexpected length of input", on short input. Before 0.6.0 the reached operation exposes UnexpectedEof, "failed to fill whole buffer", or older permissive bool behavior. Every stable 1.x release uses InvalidData instead of InvalidInput. Exactly one byte is consumed. Tags 0 and 1 decode to false and true; any other tag returns "Invalid bool representation: N" with the decimal byte N and the profile-specific error kind. Before 0.2.10 every non-1 byte is accepted as false; through 0.2.5 even empty input returns false. Success advances the slice by the scalar width. The contract deliberately leaves the remaining slice after an error unconstrained: the pinned std read_exact empties a short slice, while the predecessor and Borsh no_std implementation retain it. No additional reader callback domain is admitted by the predecessor mapping, and it does not create a registered older callable binding.

profiles.argument: All 47 helper-present stable releases correspond to the unrestricted family. Every published src/de/hint.rs body casts size_of::<T>() to u32 before evaluating 4096 / divisor, then min with the u32 hint and max with 1. The model represents that cast as size % 2^32 and represents division-by-zero through an explicit panic callback, so size 2^32 panics and size 2^32 + 1 uses divisor 1. There is no size < 2^32 premise. The helper is absent in the eight enumerated earlier releases. The three retained source-closure groups differ only in imports/formatting and share this arithmetic and order.
conditions: The index records size_of::<T>(); the binding establishes it for the actual target layout of T.
The unit-context division-panic callback interprets the actual panic strategy and effects, retaining unwind state or terminal reason. Its Empty return value rules out returning normally.
The family has no size precondition: it reduces size modulo 2^32 and invokes the panic callback for every zero divisor, including size zero and positive multiples of 2^32, even when hint is zero.

The law Index.hashShape of the index gives every answer of the environment to this request the hash shape: status below 2^64, one 32-byte digest on status 0 and no bytes otherwise; the call has no precondition. The canonical runtime meets the law by the width law of Solanalib.Runtime.Prims (sha256_length), so a canonical return is a 32-byte digest with no premise on the world (canonical_sha256_post_iff).

The argument aligned is whether vals is 8-aligned as Agave checks it, on its host translation; where the index checks alignment, a call with a slice and aligned = false does not return (Sha256Args.unaligned), as Agave aborts it before reading a descriptor.

The limit of the index Index.maxHashSlices, if any, is the limit of the environment on val_len; a call with more slices does not return (Sha256Args.overLimit), whatever its alignment, as Agave checks the count before any other check and aborts with TooManySlices. The limit of the canonical runtime is the maxHashSlices of the profile.

conditions: The index provider interprets the answers of the actual syscall environment and terminal exits for .hash .sha256 slices, with slices the bytes that the vals descriptors point to, in order, and its terminal exits for .abort as the abort of the runtime of a call that fails the slice-count check or the alignment check of vals.

The law Index.hashShape of the index gives every answer of the environment to this request the hash shape: status below 2^64, one 32-byte digest on status 0 and no bytes otherwise; the call has no precondition. The canonical runtime meets the law by the width law of Solanalib.Runtime.Prims (sha256_length), so a canonical return is a 32-byte digest with no premise on the world (canonical_sha256_post_iff).

The argument aligned is whether vals is 8-aligned as Agave checks it, on its host translation; where the index checks alignment, a call with a slice and aligned = false does not return (Sha256Args.unaligned), as Agave aborts it before reading a descriptor.

The limit of the index Index.maxHashSlices, if any, is the limit of the environment on val_len; a call with more slices does not return (Sha256Args.overLimit), whatever its alignment, as Agave checks the count before any other check and aborts with TooManySlices. The limit of the canonical runtime is the maxHashSlices of the profile.

Other tags return InvalidData / Invalid enum value before reading a body; error construction is interpreted under the shared scope boundary. Through 3.1.0 the complete nested field order, integer/address decoding, every flag byte and success remainder match the model. Delegation warmup_cooldown_rate is f64, and NaNs fail with InvalidData / For portability reasons we do not allow to deserialize NaNs. before credits_observed and the trailing flag. Version 4.0.0 replaces this field with _reserved: [u8; 8], so NaN-shaped bytes are accepted and a truncated tail after them returns the short-input error instead. Retained native cases at 4.0.0 and 5.1.1 confirm these functional differences. Accordingly the nine releases through 3.1.0 are compatible and the nine later releases are incompatible, without excluding NaNs from the input domain or adding diagnostic-allocation premises. StakeStateV2 Borsh 1 trait implementation with Borsh/derive 1.6.1 and solana-pubkey 2.4.0. The f64 delegation field is retained.

profiles.argument: No onchain module/API exists through 0.6.1. Versions 0.7.0–7.0.0 append every additional signer and do not perform the current multisig owner/size/key filter or clear authority signer status. Versions 8.0.0/8.0.1/9.0.0 have the modern local multisig wrapper, but their hook 0.10/resolver 0.10 profile preserves the signer flag of a new extra account; the model always clears it. Version 10.0.0 is compatible under the executed allowed hook 2.1/resolver 0.11.1 profile: its PodMultisig pod_from_bytes helper is exactly try_from_bytes.map_err(InvalidArgument), and its interface 2.1.0 Mint parsing/getter and instruction closures correspond. Version 11.0.0 has the same full ordinary preparation under the baseline interface 3.0.0 profile. Version 11.1.0 requires interface>=3.1.0, which removes the 83-byte repeated-zero padding allocation from extended Mint parsing. The full family includes that allocation, its possible exits and retirement; the native 4-case padding probes expose 1/1 events at 10.0/11.0 versus 0/0 at 11.1. Thus 11.1.0 and 12.0.0 do not fit the complete family despite identical top-level wrapper source and passing ordinary corpus samples. Version 12.0.0 also makes pinocchio-transfer-hook-interface 0.1.0 mandatory, forcing resolver>=0.11.4. That resolver retains one collected data-Ref vector, accumulates pending AccountInfos and borrows each resolved extra, including the last. A final extra account with exclusively held data succeeds in resolver 0.11.1 preparation but fails AccountBorrowFailed in 0.11.4 before CPI. The old profile is rejected by Cargo; this is an incompatibility for both facets, not an optional dependency choice.
